speaker: Unknown
en: All right.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Welcome, everyone.
zh: 欢迎各位。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to tell you a little bit about the new knowledge layer, and I'll start with telling you a little bit about theory of mind.
zh: 我想给大家简单介绍一下新的知识层，我先从心智理论讲起。

speaker: Unknown
en: How many of you know what theory of mind is?
zh: 你们有多少人知道什么是心智理论？

speaker: Unknown
en: All right, so a few folks.
zh: 好的，有几位。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a term in psychology about our capacity to understand and have a mental state or a model of a mental state for other people.
zh: 它是心理学中的一个术语，指的是我们理解他人并对其心理状态或心理状态模型进行建模的能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: What do they know?
zh: 他们知道什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What do they believe in?
zh: 他们相信什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: How do they act?
zh: 他们如何行动？

speaker: Unknown
en: That's what allows us to socialize.
zh: 正是这种能力让我们能够社交。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's what allows us to lie to each other and so on.
zh: 正是这种能力让我们能够互相撒谎等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it's a crucial developmental stage for humans and a necessary function.
zh: 但它是人类发展的一个关键阶段，也是一种必要的功能。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll sort of explain it in the best possible way with a funny story just to break the ice.
zh: 我想用一个有趣的故事来最好地解释它，顺便活跃一下气氛。

speaker: Unknown
en: About 15, 16 years ago, I worked at a company called Yahoo.
zh: 大约十五六年前，我在一家叫 Yahoo 的公司工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: That had a product called Yahoo Answers, which was sort of like a Q&A forum.
zh: 它有一个叫 Yahoo Answers 的产品，有点像一个问答论坛。

speaker: Unknown
en: We used then AI, which is the stone age of AI, you know, it's like NLP and other statistical models to answer questions.
zh: 我们当时用 AI——那是 AI 的石器时代，你知道，就是 NLP 和其他统计模型——来回答问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the funny thing is people would come to Yahoo and ask questions like, am I fat?
zh: 但有趣的是，人们会来到 Yahoo 问这样的问题，比如：我胖吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Which is funny because obviously a Q&A forum wouldn't have any clue whether you're too fat or not.
zh: 这很可笑，因为很显然一个问答论坛根本不可能知道你是不是太胖。

speaker: Unknown
en: But this is a funny way to say, yeah, people have a very bad theory of mind on sort of what the products that they use, what information they have and what they don't have.
zh: 但这以一种有趣的方式说明，是的，人们对自己所使用的产品拥有什么信息、没有什么信息，心智理论非常差。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I want to argue that in some sense,
zh: 而我想论证的是，在某种意义上，

speaker: Unknown
en: We are making that mistake with AI today in a more subtle and less silly way, but in a just as fundamental of a mismatch.
zh: 我们今天在 AI 上正犯着同样的错误，只是方式更微妙、不那么可笑，但同样是一种根本性的错配。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I will categorize roughly three kinds of knowledge.
zh: 所以我大致把知识分为三类。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there are many more, but in broad strokes, this is not a bad way to categorize.
zh: 我认为还有很多种，但粗略来说，这不失为一种不错的分类方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: First is general knowledge.
zh: 第一类是通用知识。

speaker: Unknown
en: Think about that is what's available in the public domain, things that models are trained on, and we expect an LLM to just know out the gate, things about just improving your Rust code, explaining stuff about the legal terms, or exploring use cases for products.
zh: 你可以把它理解为公开领域中可获得的东西，也就是模型训练时接触的内容，我们期望 LLM 开箱即知的东西，比如改进你的 Rust 代码、解释法律条款，或者探索产品的用例。

speaker: Unknown
en: We know how to do that.
zh: 我们知道怎么处理这类知识。

speaker: Unknown
en: Models are really good at that.
zh: 模型非常擅长这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: When we use our agents, they have that information.
zh: 当我们使用智能体时，它们拥有这类信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: There is specific knowledge.
zh: 还有特定知识。

speaker: Unknown
en: The companies, of course, the models wouldn't have any clue about whether we've implemented something specific in our code base, what a contract of a specific customer has.
zh: 至于公司层面的东西，模型当然完全不知道我们是否在代码库里实现了某个特定功能，某个特定客户的合同内容是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Of course, this is information that's private to the company, but we know how to deal with that.
zh: 当然，这是公司私有的信息，但我们知道怎么处理它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And RAG and Search and, of course, Pinecone, VectalDBs, and so on, solved these problems a long time ago.
zh: RAG、搜索，当然还有 Pinecone、VectalDB 等等，早就解决了这些问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's still a lot to go, but we, by and large, know how to do it.
zh: 虽然还有很多工作要做，但总体上我们知道该怎么做。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I would say there is tribal knowledge.
zh: 然后我要说的是，还有部落知识。

speaker: Unknown
en: Tribal knowledge is the general knowledge inside the company.
zh: 部落知识是公司内部的通用知识。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is the kind of information that a seasoned employee has that a new hire does not.
zh: 这是资深员工拥有而新员工没有的那类信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's roughly how we do things, what our processes are, who's in charge of what, what are the guiding principles, how we get stuff done in this company.
zh: 它大致上就是：我们怎么做事、我们的流程是什么、谁负责什么、指导原则是什么、我们在这家公司如何把事情办成。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's not general knowledge because it's specific to your company, but it's also not a specific piece of knowledge because you can't just get it by searching.
zh: 它不是通用知识，因为它是你的公司特有的，但它也不是特定知识，因为你没法只靠搜索就得到它。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can't just get it by plucking it off one place and say, yes, this document says that this is our culture.
zh: 你不能只是从某个地方捞出来就说：好，这份文件写着这就是我们的文化。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's the sum total of a lot of things.
zh: 它是很多事物的总和。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so our theory of mind of most of our agents in big companies today should be something like a new hire.
zh: 所以，如今大公司里大多数智能体的心智理论应该类似于一个新员工。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're brilliant, they have tools, we have very high expectations of them, but they are by and large clueless.
zh: 他们很聪明，他们有工具，我们对他们期望很高，但他们大体上是一头雾水的。

speaker: Unknown
en: They have no idea about your company's goals, culture, priorities, processes.
zh: 他们对你的公司的目标、文化、优先级、流程一无所知。

speaker: Unknown
en: They have to read a bunch of documents to be able to get any semblance of understanding of where they are in the world.
zh: 他们必须阅读一大堆文档，才能对自己身处什么样的世界有一点点理解。

speaker: Unknown
en: And really, they start most tasks from scratch.
zh: 而且说实话，他们大多数任务都是从零开始的。

speaker: Unknown
en: They really start to wake up, and every time you start your session, they're like a new hire on their first day on the job.
zh: 他们真的每次都是刚醒来，而且每次你开启一个新会话，他们就像上班第一天的应届新员工。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I would argue that what they need is not necessarily to be smarter, to have better tools, but to have something new, which I would call a knowledge layer going forward.
zh: 所以我认为，他们需要的未必是变得更聪明、拥有更好的工具，而是需要某种新的东西，我接下来称之为知识层。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I have to explain to you what I think a knowledge layer has to actually do.
zh: 而我必须向你们解释，我认为知识层究竟必须做什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just I'll define it generally before I explain to you what we do.
zh: 在解释我们做了什么之前，我先给它下一个一般性的定义。

speaker: Unknown
en: So at the very least, it needs to be persistent.
zh: 那么，至少，它需要是持久的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We talked about this as the company knowledge, processes, capabilities, and goals, and so on.
zh: 我们把这称为公司的知识、流程、能力和目标等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: It has to be persistent.
zh: 它必须是持久的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It feels like putting this thing together is going to be a monumental effort.
zh: 感觉上,把这个东西拼起来将是一项巨大的工程。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you want to do it once, or at least very rarely.
zh: 所以你会想只做一次,或者至少很少重做。

speaker: Unknown
en: And of course, all your agents in a company need to have access to this thing.
zh: 而且当然,公司里所有的智能体都需要能访问这个东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: The second thing is that you would argue that this knowledge layer needs to be highly specialized.
zh: 第二点是,你会主张这个知识层需要高度专业化。

speaker: Unknown
en: If your agent is in charge of HR practices or optimizing your kernels in your code base or resolving customer issues, that they would care about different things.
zh: 如果你的智能体负责 HR 实践,或者优化代码库里的内核,或者解决客户问题,它们关心的东西是不同的。

speaker: Unknown
en: They would want to have different information available to them.
zh: 它们会希望有不同的信息可供使用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I would argue, irrelevant of specifically how it's created, I would argue that it's a good practice to have the domain experts in the company own those and being able to interact with them and make sure that they actually are aligned with what the company wants to do.
zh: 而且我认为,不管它具体是怎么创建的,让公司里的领域专家拥有这些东西,并能够与它们交互,确保它们真正与公司想做的事情保持一致,是一个好的实践。

speaker: Unknown
en: And finally, which is the hardest thing is they need to stay up to date and they need to stay concurrent constantly because companies change and you need to make information deprecated when it becomes deprecated.
zh: 最后,也是最难的一点是,它们需要保持最新,并且需要持续保持并发,因为公司会变化,当信息过时的时候,你需要让它被弃用。

speaker: Unknown
en: If the company replaces its CEO,
zh: 如果公司更换了 CEO,

speaker: Unknown
en: The very next day, everybody in the company knows who the CEO is.
zh: 第二天,公司里的每个人都知道新的 CEO 是谁。

speaker: Unknown
en: Even though 9,000 documents going from a day before yesterday to the last 10 years say it's somebody else, this has become common tribal knowledge immediately.
zh: 尽管从前天到过去 10 年的 9000 份文档都说 CEO 是另外某个人,但这立刻变成了共同的部落知识。

speaker: Unknown
en: And everything else, even every RAG search will tell you otherwise, this is now the overriding fact.
zh: 其他一切,甚至每一次 RAG 搜索都会告诉你相反的结果,而现在这才是压倒一切的事实。

speaker: Unknown
en: I will argue before we move on that I'm not suggesting that this knowledge layer should replace everything else we're doing.
zh: 在继续之前我要说明,我并不是在说这个知识层应该取代我们正在做的其他一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our agents are already very capable and should keep being very capable.
zh: 我们的智能体已经非常能干,并且应该继续保持非常能干。

speaker: Unknown
en: They have access to LLMs, of course, tooling, local files.
zh: 它们当然能访问 LLM、工具、本地文件。

speaker: Unknown
en: Search, of course, like RAG, Vectal Search, Text Search, and so on.
zh: 还有搜索,当然,比如 RAG、Vectal 搜索、文本搜索等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I would argue that the knowledge there needs to be a separate entity that all these agents have access to, as I explained why this is sort of a fundamentally different kind of data source.
zh: 而且我认为,那里的知识需要是一个独立的实体,所有这些智能体都能访问它,正如我解释过的,为什么这是一种本质上不同类型的数据源。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I want to tell you more about Nexus.
zh: 所以我想多讲讲 Nexus。

speaker: Unknown
en: Nexus is a product that we're, of course, it's a knowledge layer, but I want to explain to you what it does.
zh: Nexus 是我们正在做的一个产品,当然,它是一个知识层,但我想向你解释它是做什么的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Of course, so the four parts are roughly connectors, what I would call context tasks and queries.
zh: 当然,它大致有四个部分:连接器、我称之为上下文的任务和查询。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll explain each one of them.
zh: 我会逐一解释。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, so Connectos, of course, do the obvious things.
zh: 那么,连接器当然做那些显而易见的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's nothing much to talk about them.
zh: 关于它们没什么好多谈的。

speaker: Unknown
en: They bring data into the platform, respect access rights and control and so on.
zh: 它们把数据带入平台,尊重访问权限和控制等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: Very dull as a topic of discussion, but incredibly important in enterprises, incredibly important to do right, and everybody who's built that knows how painstaking it is to get this thing to work well.
zh: 作为讨论话题非常枯燥,但在企业中极其重要,极其需要做对,每个构建过这个的人都明白让这东西良好运作有多费劲。

speaker: Unknown
en: The interesting, sort of the first properly interesting part is the context.
zh: 有意思的,算是第一个真正有意思的部分是上下文。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the context, think about that as the sum of assets that the Nexus or this knowledge layer saves about a specific topic.
zh: 上下文,把它想成 Nexus 或这个知识层保存的、关于某个特定主题的资产总和。

speaker: Unknown
en: Think about this as a context for HR, for operations, for engineering, and so on.
zh: 把它想成 HR 的上下文、运营的上下文、工程的上下文等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: Of course, it has the sources, the connections to the data, and so on.
zh: 当然,它有数据源、与数据的连接等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: But then it has the manifest.
zh: 但它还有 manifest。

speaker: Unknown
en: The manifest is the first truly novel idea in an important entity.
zh: Manifest 是第一个真正新颖的想法,在一个重要的实体里。

speaker: Unknown
en: The way that we today give context to our agents is with skills and plug-ins and commands and markdown, fuzzy, write ourselves.
zh: 我们今天给智能体提供上下文的方式,是用技能、插件、命令和 markdown,模糊地、自己动手写。

speaker: Unknown
en: In a knowledge layer, you don't do that anymore.
zh: 在知识层里,你不再那么做了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You tell the knowledge layer, you tell Nexus what you care about in a manifest.
zh: 你告诉知识层,你在 manifest 里告诉 Nexus 你关心什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: You say what kind of tasks you want to complete, what entities you want to track, what kind of information you care about.
zh: 你说你想要完成什么样的任务,你想追踪哪些实体,你关心什么样的信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's the knowledge layer's work to keep track of those files and organize its own data.
zh: 而追踪那些文件并组织它自己的数据,是知识层的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then it has the knowledge files themselves.
zh: 然后它还有知识文件本身。

speaker: Unknown
en: So think about the manifest as the meta knowledge file or set of files.
zh: 所以把 manifest 想成元知识文件或一组文件。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then there's the knowledge.
zh: 然后是知识。

speaker: Unknown
en: The knowledge itself, think about this as five types of
zh: 知识本身,把它想成五种类型

speaker: Unknown
en: The first kind is a semantic map.
zh: 第一种叫语义地图。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is a file that organizes the catalog of where everything else is, the key schemas, the glossaries, all the information that you need to be able to operate this context.
zh: 这是一个文件,组织所有其他东西所在位置的目录、关键 schema、术语表,你操作这个上下文所需的全部信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then there are, of course, a bunch of markdown files that contain information, decisions, memories, all sorts of unstructured information.
zh: 然后,当然,有一堆 markdown 文件,包含信息、决策、记忆,各种非结构化的信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: Who here has heard about LLMWiki?
zh: 在座的谁听说过 LLMWiki?

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, so LLMWiki is this idea that Andrei Karpathy suggested to have agents basically manage some stash of markdown files to sort of keep their own notes of stuff.
zh: 好,LLMWiki 是 Andrei Karpathy 提出的这个想法,让智能体基本上管理一批 markdown 文件,给自己记一些笔记之类。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is a very similar idea.
zh: 这是一个非常类似的想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: OK, sort of on steroids, but a similar concept.
zh: 好,算是在此基础上加强了,但概念类似。

speaker: Unknown
en: But that's not enough.
zh: 但这还不够。

speaker: Unknown
en: Context contains also a bunch of SQL tables for tabular data, for aggregation, for facts that they need to memorize, a vector database to be able to semantically search and text search and filter a bunch of information and all the information that it itself decides is necessary to keep and remember, and graph entities and graph indexes to remember, again, entities, relationships, causal chains, and so on.
zh: 上下文中还包含一堆 SQL 表格,用于表格数据、聚合、需要记住的事实,还有一个向量数据库,能够进行语义搜索、文本搜索和过滤大量信息,以及所有由它自己决定有必要保留和记住的信息,还有图实体和图索引,用来记住实体、关系、因果链等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: And all of that is managed and created for you.
zh: 而所有这些都是为你管理和创建好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't touch any of this.
zh: 你不用碰任何这些。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't have to know how any of this is created.
zh: 你不需要知道这些是如何创建的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's all maintained through the manifest.
zh: 一切都通过 manifest 来维护。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, this is the context.
zh: 它基本上用简单的函数抽象了对那些信息的所有访问,这样我等一下会讲到的智能体就不必知道如何访问上下文的内部部件。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, what are the tasks?
zh: 那么,任务是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: What are the actions?
zh: 动作是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: These are the nouns.
zh: 这些是名词。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are the verbs?
zh: 动词是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: What can we do with those objects?
zh: 我们能对这些对象做什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: First of all is, of course, import, which is bring new information in the system, new files, new events, new concepts.
zh: 首先是,当然是 import(导入),也就是把新信息带进系统,新文件、新事件、新概念。

speaker: Unknown
en: Curate is probably the most and most elaborate, it's one of the two most elaborate functions.
zh: Curate(整理)可能是最——它是最精细的、是两个最精细的函数之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: Its job is to take
zh: 它的工作是拿取

speaker: Unknown
en: To take the, say, call it a file.
zh: 拿取,比如说,姑且叫它一个文件。

speaker: Unknown
en: It doesn't have to be a file.
zh: 它不一定非得是文件。

speaker: Unknown
en: But let's say it's a new PDF or a new meeting transcription or a new presentation for the board and say, now I need to update my view of the world.
zh: 但假设它是一份新 PDF,或一份新的会议转写稿,或一份给董事会的新演示文稿,然后说,现在我要更新我对世界的认知了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it takes that.
zh: 于是它拿到那个东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: It takes the manifest, which tells, okay, now what things do I care about?
zh: 它拿到 manifest,manifest 告诉它,好,现在我在乎哪些东西?

speaker: Unknown
en: What concepts do I need to track?
zh: 哪些概念是我需要追踪的?

speaker: Unknown
en: What do I need to memorize here?
zh: 我在这里需要记住什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: And then it takes the semantic map that I told you contains, organizes where information is and understands, OK, fine, I need to go update these tables, these relationships to my graph, these text indexes, and so on.
zh: 然后它拿到我刚才告诉过你的语义地图,其中组织了信息的位置,并理解,好,行,我需要去更新这些表格、这些关系到我的图的关系、这些文本索引,等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when it's done, it has essentially said, OK, fine, I have assimilated the new information.
zh: 当它完成后,基本上就是说,好,行,我已经消化了新信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's sort of persisted in your context, and we can move on.
zh: 它某种程度上已经持久化到你的上下文里了,我们可以继续了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Search is sort of an internal function, very important.
zh: Search(搜索)算是一个内部函数,非常重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: It basically abstracts with simple functions all the access to that information so that the agent that I'll tell you in a second doesn't have to know how to access the internal parts of the context.
zh: 它基本上用简单的函数抽象了对那些信息的所有访问,这样我马上会讲到的智能体就不需要知道如何访问上下文的内部部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now comes the second, I think, most interesting part of the system.
zh: 接下来是系统的第二个,我认为,最有意思的部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: Which is NoQL.
zh: 那就是 NoQL。

speaker: Unknown
en: NoQL is our way to specify how we want information out of the context.
zh: NoQL 是我们用来指定如何从上下文中取出信息的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not enough to just ask questions.
zh: 仅仅提问是不够的。

speaker: Unknown
